stages.title: Setting out
stages.line: Travel light, come home, turn round, find company.
stages.why: Every journey starts by putting something down and finding who walks with you.

stages.title: Seeing others
stages.line: Right anger, the person at the gate, the wounded on the road.
stages.why: Once you have set out, the first thing that changes is what you notice.

stages.title: Love that comes first
stages.line: Loved before you earn it; asked, met with joy, free to question.
stages.why: Before anything is asked of you, you are loved. Everything else rests on that.

stages.title: Holding steady
stages.line: Making peace, keeping faith, opening the door.
stages.why: Now the road gets harder: provocation, pressure, strangers.

stages.title: Looking back on the road
stages.why: Like the friends at Emmaus, you see the road best when you look back on it.

stages.title: Learning to pray
stages.line: Daily bread, a cry, a voice in the field, not my will.
stages.why: Having looked back on the road, you learn to speak to the one who walked it with you.

stages.title: Witnesses
stages.line: People who stood where it cost them something.
stages.why: Prayer turns outward: you meet those who kept faith in public, and the great crowd at All Saints.

stages.title: Death and hope
stages.line: Graves, grief, and a door that opens.
stages.why: November remembers the dead. Having met the witnesses, you face what they faced: the end, and what lies past it.

stages.title: Justice and mercy
stages.why: Hope beyond death changes how you treat the living: fairly, and with mercy.

stages.title: The kingdom
stages.why: Justice and mercy add up to a kingdom. The church year ends by asking who really rules.

stages.title: Waiting
stages.line: Shut in the ark, watching in the temple.
stages.why: At the turn of the year, the old calendar teaches you to wait well.

stages.title: Prepare the way
stages.line: A voice in the wilderness; what should we do?
stages.why: Advent begins. Waiting becomes getting ready.

stages.title: Light in darkness
stages.line: The longest nights, and a light on the road.
stages.why: As the days shorten, the stories are of light breaking into the dark.

stages.title: God comes close
stages.line: Joseph, Mary, Zechariah and the road to Bethlehem.
stages.why: The light has a face. The last days of Advent bring you to the people closest to the birth.

stages.title: Christmas
stages.why: Everything on the path has led here: God with us, in a manger.
